title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The improved wellbeing of vulnerable Syrian refugee and host communities programme in Lebanon implemented by Concern Worldwide aims to build safe and resilient communities and to prevent any type of violence against women, men, girls and boys with a specific focus on women and children at risk or exposed to violence. The objectives of the programme is to take a holistic family approach, working with partners, to prevent against early marriage, child labour and SGBV. The key activities include Engaging Men sessions to improve the relationship with their children; and focussed psychosocial sessions for children and persons at heightened protection risk i.e unaccompanied and separated children; persons with special legal or physical protection needs; women-headed households; persons with disabilities; and persons of diverse sex, sexual orientation or gender identity. Cash assistance is provided for individuals with identified protection risks.. Concern works with two national partners, one for Child Protection (CP) and another for Gender-Based Violence (GBV). Concern supports the two partners under CHC through a comprehensive capacity‑strengthening package, including training in gender‑responsive, child‑sensitive, and disability‑inclusive case management, strengthened referral pathways and cross‑sector coordination, and enhanced accountability, monitoring, and data management systems.
